subject: Follow-up: data responsibilities & breach routing (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dwyer <alex.dwyer@helixhealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: data responsibilities & breach routing (post-demo)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can qualify next steps with Legal & Security on both sides.

Recap (short):
- Goal: HelixHealth prototype for claims triage — limited PII in inputs (name, DOB, limited PHI in notes).
- Mode: Hosted Redwood API initially; potential Dedicated later for throughput.

Open items Helix asked about (please confirm):
1) Controller vs. Processor: you flagged wanting explicit language in the DPA — can you confirm whether Helix will require a controller-controller carveout or simply standard controller (Helix) / processor (Redwood) assignment?
2) Subprocessors & notification: what advance notice window for new subprocessors do you need? 30 days?  — also whether Helix requires the right to object.
3) Breach notice timing: you mentioned wanting an aggressive timeline in the call. What is Helix’s desired initial notification SLA (e.g., initial acknowledgement within 24h) and final incident report timeline (72h / 7 days)?
4) Data residency & residency proof: confirm whether US-only residency is required (or EU+US). If EU data must stay in-region, we’ll propose Dedicated/Private options and a residency attestation.
5) Logging & retention: sample logs and current default retention window (we typically retain request/trace logs 90 days for hosted; customizable for Dedicated/Private). What retention window do you need for audit?

Next steps from our side: I’ve requested a redline DPA + SOC2 summary from Legal & Security and can share sample log extracts. Can you loop in legal@helixhealth.com on this thread so we have formal redline circulation?

If helpful I can propose an hour with Alex + Helix Legal + Rishi (security) next week to walk the DPA line-by-line. Please confirm your preferred cadence.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment stubs: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20290521.pdf (redline), Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20290521.pdf (report summary), sample_logging_extract.csv (CSV sample)

From: Alex Dwyer <alex.dwyer@helixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@helixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data responsibilities & breach routing (post-demo)

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Looping in legal as requested. Quick answers and clarifying Qs:

- Controller/Processor: Helix will be Controller; Redwood Processor. We do not expect a controller-controller model. We will want explicit processor obligations in the addendum (data segregation, access controls, subprocessors list).

- Subprocessors: Helix Legal generally asks for 30 days advance notice and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors. If you have a published subprocessor register that’s fine; for any change that affects EU residency we will require notification and the ability to pause onboarding until review.

- Breach notification: Initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of Redwood becoming aware is our preferred baseline; a substantive incident summary within 72 hours; full forensics/lessons-learned within 30 days. If you can commit to that cadence, that helps procurement.

- Residency: We need EU-hosted data to stay within the EU (for EU-originated records). For US-originated records we prefer US-only residency. Please confirm whether you can pin residency per-tenant for hosted vs Dedicated.

- Logging & retention: For audit we typically need 12 months of logs for access and usage (also chain-of-custody). If 12 months is not feasible for hosted, tell us the options (Dedicated/Private with extended retention).

Also: please share SOC2 Type II (or summary) and a DPA redline. We’ll have Legal review and come back with any redlines.

Alex
Alex Dwyer | Head of Product Security, HelixHealth
alex.dwyer@helixhealth.com | (206) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Follow-up: data responsibilities & breach routing (post-demo)

Marissa / Alex — I’m Rishi (Security & Privacy). Quick clarifications from Redwood’s side and what we can share today.

1) Controller / Processor
- Redwood accepts Processor role in the DPA. We will not seek controller designation for hosted inference. Standard obligations will be in the DPA (processing instructions, assistance with subject requests, deletion on termination).

2) Subprocessors
- We maintain a current subprocessor register in the Console (link below). We typically provide 30 days’ notice for a planned subprocessor addition. For high-risk changes impacting residency we will flag and coordinate with customers and pause onboarding where feasible. Helix’s right to object can be included for named high-risk subprocessors; we’ve accepted that in enterprise deals before.

3) Breach notification timing
- Initial acknowledgement: we can commit to sending an initial incident acknowledgement within 24 hours of Redwood becoming aware of an event affecting customer data.
- Substantive incident summary / scope: target within 72 hours where feasible.
- Full root-cause & forensics: delivered as available, typically within 30 days; some complex incidents may require longer and we will communicate timelines.

4) Data residency & pinning
- Hosted (shared) tenants: we can offer region-specific tenancy for EU-only or US-only where required for customers; however, EU pinning for shared hosted tenants requires a Dedicated or Private deployment for stricter guarantees. We can provide residency attestation for Dedicated and Private deployments.

5) Logging & retention
- Default hosted retention: request+trace logs retained 90 days.
- Dedicated/Private: configurable retention up to 12 months or longer on request (operational and storage tradeoffs apply). We can provide sample logs today for your audit team.

Attachments we are including in this thread (stubs):
- Redwood_DPA_Redline_20290521.pdf (legal redline against standard DPA)
- Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20290521.pdf (SOC2 Type II summary and scope)
- sample_logging_extract.csv (anonymized sample of request/trace logs)

Operational note: if Helix needs 12-month log retention on hosted, we’ll typically propose Dedicated with extended retention as the commercial path. If that’s acceptable we can put a commercial note in the proposal.

If Helix Legal is comfortable with the notification cadence and subprocessors approach above I recommend we set a focused call (30–45m) to walk the redline. I can join along with Jonas for privacy specifics.

— Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
